ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g4-arts-music-u01-l03

Lesson focus: space and composition

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — first supported pass for space and composition. 1 INTENT: name what the study should do. 2 SETUP: choose a safe, available route. 3 NOTICE: locate placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction. 4 ACT: complete one small study using this cue—A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops. 5 CHECK: point to the result before using “works” or “does not work.” 6 SECOND STUDY: change one relationship only. Keep both attempts and circle the exact prompt you are ready to remove. Worked example for space and composition: A small dark isolated form can lead a large pale form because the local value jump and open space are stronger than size alone. Use it to study space and composition; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses things you look at (space and composition). You may use raised or textured materials, very large print, strong colours, or a spoken description instead.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.fallback: Use the complete adjacent verbal description and recreate the relationships with raised or movable paper forms. The required Academy model is attached; no outside search is needed.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce space and composition to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one placement relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact placement evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply space and composition under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on space and composition rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

the area intended as the strongest or first stop

concept_instruction.title: What space and composition means here
concept_instruction.body: Visual hierarchy is the order in which a composition invites attention.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A steep hierarchy reads quickly but can silence later areas. A shallow hierarchy can feel open but may make a precise route harder to read. Worked example: A small dark isolated form can lead a large pale form because the local value jump and open space are stronger than size alone. Non-example: Making every edge, colour, and value equally strong creates competition rather than a controllable path.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for space and composition is present, but the record does not yet locate placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
